These fixtures validate preprocessing independently of Rust inference.

`preprocess.json` contains 12 Pillow bicubic resize hashes and nine complete
two-stage resize/patch-packing cases. The source RGB pattern is deterministic,
with independent channel values and high-frequency content. Cases exercise
upscaling, downscaling, horizontal-only/vertical-only resizing, single-pixel
dimensions, Python ties-to-even alignment, and the processor's minimum-area rule.
Both resize pixels and normalized FP32 patches are checked exactly.

Regenerate from the repository root after fetching the pinned model:

```powershell
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04-CUDA --cd /mnt/c/Users/amazi/Documents/ChatGPT/falcon-ocr -- /home/amazi/falcon-ocr-rust-reference/.venv/bin/python tests/generate_preprocess_fixtures.py
cargo test --lib preprocess
cargo test --lib tokenizer -- --include-ignored
```

The checked-in metadata identifies Pillow 12.3.0, NumPy 2.5.1, PyTorch
2.11.0+cu130 and the processor source checksum. Generation only uses CPU tensors.
The generator extracts the two pure dimension/resize helpers from the actual
pinned source; it does not require importing the complete Transformers model.
The separate GPU reference export validates the published processor end to end.

Spatial coordinates need a numerical comparison. PyTorch's CPU square root
calls MKL VML with high accuracy, which can differ from an IEEE correctly rounded
FP32 square root. The independent reference uses NumPy's FP32 square root and
explicit fused, endpoint-anchored linspace. Before comparing Rust, the generator
records each case's maximum absolute discrepancy and diagnostic ULP difference
between those independent references. Across these nine fixtures the maximum is
`5.960464477539063e-8` (two ULP in a resulting coordinate). All other cases have
zero discrepancy. Rust must exactly match the independent coordinate hashes and
stay within each case's measured bound against PyTorch. These observations do
not establish a universal tolerance for arbitrary images or backends.

`decode.json` and `images/` add 75 file-input preprocessing cases generated by
`tests/generate_decode_fixtures.py` with the same pinned Pillow runtime: 39 PNG
cases and 36 JPEG cases, each covering no first resize, upscaling, and downscaling.
PNG fixtures include RGB, grayscale, one-bit, palette, transparency metadata,
RGBA/LA, and 16-bit grayscale/RGB/alpha. JPEG fixtures include grayscale, CMYK,
progressive encoding, qualities 10/75/100, and chroma subsampling 4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0.
All final FP32 patch buffers are compared exactly. The 12 JPEG files additionally
have exact decoded RGB comparisons against their `.jpg.rgb` reference bytes.

The default image crate JPEG decoder differed from Pillow by up to three levels
on these RGB fixtures. The runner therefore uses vendored libjpeg-turbo 3.1.0
(through turbojpeg 1.5.1 / turbojpeg-sys 1.2.0) with accurate IDCT and fancy chroma
upsampling. It matches the pinned Pillow libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4.1 fixtures exactly.
Source modes are retained until after the first resize: palette/one-bit images
use nearest sampling, alpha images use premultiplication, 16-bit grayscale is
resampled at 16-bit precision then clipped during RGB conversion, and CMYK JPEG
channels are resized before the RGB conversion. No blanket equivalence claim is
made for untested bitstreams or uncommon codec features.

Windows builds/tests can use the local-tool bootstrap wrapper:

```powershell
./tools/build_windows.ps1 -CargoArguments @('test','--lib','preprocess')
```

Linux uses `bash tools/build_linux.sh test --lib preprocess`. Both wrappers
find installed tools or fetch checksum-verified local NASM/CMake copies. Linux
requires an existing C compiler and GNU make; Windows requires MSVC Build Tools.
Tool downloads do not modify global environment configuration.
